project.name: GhostKey
project.runtimeConstraint: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, Vercel, browser Web Workers
project.architectureConstraint: local-first core with server-side Gemini candidate-rerank proxy and local fallback

designPhilosophy: GhostKey should feel like a friendly multi-method cryptanalysis web app first, with the Autokey simulator available as the coursework support path. The interface must make Bypass evidence visible without becoming a forced hacker console.
currentScopeDecision: Bypass Tool is now the primary product concept for Auto Detect, classical ciphers, toy asymmetric parameters, and JWT checks. Autokey Cipher encrypt/decrypt remains a sufficient grading-safe simulator with Encrypt & Send, Decrypt Message, Reset, Alice-Eve-Bob states, and formula rows.

conceptualAnchor.name: classroom-evidence-bench
conceptualAnchor.specificReferencePoint: A teacher demonstrates an unknown artifact by measuring signals, routing methods, and locking evidence to the strongest candidate
conceptualAnchor.rationale: The Bypass Tool must handle multiple weak methods without turning into generic dashboard chrome or offensive-console theater.
conceptualAnchor.signatureMotion: evidence lock-in with method, trace, confidence, and finding aligned to the current best candidate
conceptualAnchor.typographicDecision: readable sans for lesson copy, monospaced text only for keys, ciphertext, formulas, scores, and logs
conceptualAnchor.visualRiskBudget: high distinctiveness with strict readability and reduced-motion fallbacks
conceptualAnchor.motionRiskBudget: medium-high motion for progress and state changes only

distinctiveMoves: Bypass Tool starts as the main multi-method bench
Eve shows confusion after ciphertext interception
Bob reveals plaintext only after decryption
conclusion panels are split into weakness, evidence, fix, and modern alternative
Bypass panels keep the same light learning palette instead of falling back to gray forensic boxes
Short ciphertext produces capped confidence and caveats instead of overconfident magic
Bypass defaults to ciphertext-only attack mode, with optional crib evidence separated into its own control state
Autokey stays available as a sufficient coursework simulator instead of the whole product identity
Gemini AI decision runs after local plaintext candidates and can accept, mark ambiguous, or reject the final plaintext promotion without claiming proof
Toy RSA, toy ElGamal, and JWT findings skip Gemini language decision because they are structured audit outputs

derivedTokenLogic.colorDerivationSource: Semantic colors derive from evidence roles: blue for active method and learning controls, coral for weak or intercepted artifacts, green for recovered or verified candidates, amber for caveats, and ink for readable text.
derivedTokenLogic.spacingDerivationSource: Spacing follows evidence-bench clarity: input, method selector, trace, finding, and simulator controls stay grouped by task.
derivedTokenLogic.typographyDerivationSource: Readable sans supports classroom explanation; monospaced typography is reserved for keys, ciphertext, formulas, scores, hashes, and logs.
derivedTokenLogic.motionDerivationSource: Motion derives from evidence lock-in: better candidates align method state, trace log, confidence, and findings; Autokey handoff remains a secondary simulator motion.
derivedTokenLogic.validationRule: Every token must support method selection, classroom explanation, role clarity, local privacy, breach progress, or remediation clarity. Decorative tokens without product function are invalid.

aiSafeUiAudit.failureDefinition: The UI fails if it becomes a forced hacker console, generic dashboard, equal card grid, or decorative page without multi-method evidence behavior.
aiSafeUiAudit.interchangeabilityTest: If GhostKey can be renamed to a generic analytics dashboard or hacker-themed toy without changing composition, palette, method evidence, confidence caveats, and simulator behavior, the design must be revised.
requiredProductSpecificSignals: worker progress terminal with candidate keys and fitness scores
security conclusion bands tied to exploit evidence and remediation
Autokey sender-observer-receiver simulation with friendly CSS characters, Eve confusion, Bob reveal, reset, and formula rows for Pi, Ki, and Ci
short-artifact confidence caps for complex heuristic solvers
light Bypass Tool panels, history rows, terminal feed, and finding blocks
ciphertext-only mode marker plus optional crib controls only when explicitly selected
multi-method Bypass roster visible as the main product surface
AI decision caveat and local fallback visible when Gemini accepts, marks ambiguous, or rejects local plaintext candidates
Rejected plaintext candidates remain visible as reviewed candidates without being promoted as final results
AI refinement attempts are labeled as unverified language guesses, not recovered plaintext
Structured audit outputs are not sent to Gemini language scoring even when they expose a plaintextPreview display field

libraryDecisions.purpose: Application routing, page structure, and optional route handlers.
libraryDecisions.stableVersion: use create-next-app latest at implementation time
libraryDecisions.risk: Project has no package manifest yet, so exact version must be selected during scaffold.
libraryDecisions.fallbackIfUnavailable: Pause implementation and re-check official Next.js setup docs.

libraryDecisions.stableVersion: use current official Next.js install path at implementation time
libraryDecisions.risk: Token discipline is required so utilities do not bypass semantic design roles.
libraryDecisions.fallbackIfUnavailable: Use CSS modules with the same token structure.

libraryDecisions.purpose: Run expensive cryptanalysis without freezing the UI.
libraryDecisions.risk: Worker payloads must stay structured-clone safe and cancellable.
libraryDecisions.fallbackIfUnavailable: Use chunked main-thread execution with strict yielding only as a temporary degraded path.

libraryDecisions.purpose: Target deployment platform for the Next.js application.
libraryDecisions.risk: Serverless routes should not run unbounded cryptanalysis jobs.
libraryDecisions.fallbackIfUnavailable: Deploy as a static/browser-heavy Next.js app on another host after revising deployment docs.

mathSystems.typographyScaleRatio: minor-third for UI hierarchy with compact terminal rows

mutationRules.mobile: Stack by task sequence: input, module and limits, run status, result, explanation. Advanced settings collapse.
mutationRules.tablet: Pair input with live status, then show results below. Avoid cloning desktop columns.
mutationRules.desktop: Use an instrument bench: input left, terminal center, findings and conclusion right.

stateBehaviors.progress: terminal append and subtle module pulse

motionSystem.reducedMotionFallback: replace sweeps and pulses with immediate state and text updates

components.terminal: fixed-height evidence event stream with stable row dimensions
components.inputWell: secure inspection tray with loaded, focused, invalid, and empty states
components.assistedBypassEvidence: ciphertext-only by default; compact local-only known plaintext, crib, and key-length controls appear only in optional crib attack mode
components.autokeySimulation: two-action sender-observer-receiver lesson with CSS characters, Eve confusion, Bob reveal, reset, and formula rows from the active Autokey transform
components.moduleSwitcher: instrument selector with risk labels and input expectations
components.findingRow: ranked evidence row with confidence and key candidate
components.aiRerankPanel: Gemini language decision support that accepts, marks ambiguous, rejects, or cautiously refines local classical/transposition plaintext candidates while structured audit outputs stay local
components.conclusionBand: weakness, evidence, fix, and modern alternative

designExecutionHandoff.primaryExperienceGoal: Run a controlled multi-method Bypass analysis, inspect live progress, and understand the weakness and fix.

surfacePlan.role: multi-method Bypass roster and Auto Detect entry
show worker progress and candidate evidence
coursework encryption and decryption simulator with visible keystream, Encrypt & Send, Decrypt Message, Reset, and sender-observer-receiver simulation

nodes.role: explain Autokey encrypt, intercept, decrypt, sender, observed ciphertext, receiver, confusion state, reveal state, and formula values
why weak and how to fix

requiredSurfaceActions: place Bypass input and run action first
keep Autokey simulator behind its tab
show latest status before full log

interactionStateMatrix.notes: Must communicate running and cancellable states without relying on color alone.
Must keep stable height and expose updates to assistive technology.

taskFlowNarrative: Entry: user chooses an attack vector and provides an artifact.
Process: worker emits progress events while UI keeps controls responsive.
Resolution: user inspects ranked findings and reads why the artifact is weak and how to fix it.
designExecutionHandoff.signatureMoveRationale: The message handoff makes encryption and decryption visible: Eve receives unreadable ciphertext first, then Bob reveals plaintext only after decryption.

dimensions.question: Does the UI read as a friendly cryptography learning app rather than a forced hacker console or generic dashboard?
Do UI choices follow the classroom evidence bench anchor and local worker-flow contract?
Are contrast, focus, target size, keyboard access, and dynamic status access preserved?
Does motion clarify progress and state instead of decorating the page?

experiencePrinciples: Show learning state as evidence, not theater.
Explain every successful breach with a fix.
Keep sensitive artifacts local by default.
Use dense layouts only when they improve learning clarity or evidence scanning.
Treat accessibility and reduced motion as part of the instrument design.
requiredDesignSections: Spacing, Layout Rhythm, and Density Strategy
Responsive Strategy and Cross-Viewport Adaptation Matrix
Implementation Notes for Future UI Tasks

implementationEvidence: Caesar, JWT, and auto-detect MVP paths exist
Classroom breach paths now target Caesar, Reverse, Monoalphabetic, Column, Vigenere, Autokey, RSA toy keys, and ElGamal toy groups
Autokey coursework path includes a two-action sender-observer-receiver simulation with Eve confusion, Bob reveal, reset, and formula table
Text scoring uses documented self-authored English and Indonesian corpus assets in src/lib/crypto-analysis/language-corpora.ts and docs/corpus-assets.md
Auto Detect now accepts strong Caesar and Reverse evidence early, then caps complex solver confidence on short artifacts to reduce false certainty
Bypass Tool styling now uses explicit light learning surfaces for findings, history, terminal feed, meters, and spectrum bars

Gemini AI rerank uses POST /api/ai-rerank, calls Vertex AI with server-side service account credentials, returns accept/ambiguous/reject decisions for plaintext candidates, and falls back to local scoring
